answer.answer:
Two firms stand out as repeat collaborators across multiple robotic construction processes, while everyone else in this set appears in only a single joint development. Firm_060 is the most active, showing up in four separate co-development cases with four different sets of partners, and Firm_082 appears in two cases with two different partners.

Firm_060 co-developed construction robots in four documented cases, each with a different partner or partner group: with Firm_073 and Firm_008 in census_RXM6-11, where Firm_060, Firm_073, and Firm_008 jointly developed a construction robot [1]; with Firm_015 and Firm_062 in census_RXM6-8, where Firm_060, Firm_015, and Firm_062 jointly developed a construction robot [2]; with Firm_034 in census_RXM6-16, where Firm_060 and Firm_034 jointly developed a construction robot [3]; and with Firm_030 in census_RXM6-10, where Firm_060 and Firm_030 jointly developed a construction robot [4].

Firm_082 co-developed construction robots in two documented cases: with Firm_072 in census_RXM8-3, where Firm_082 and Firm_072 jointly developed a construction robot [5], and with Firm_003 in census_RXM8-1, where Firm_003 and Firm_082 jointly developed a construction robot [6].

All other firms in this set (Firm_168, Firm_054, Firm_001, Firm_177, Firm_002, Firm_018, Firm_068, Firm_094, Firm_134, Firm_209, Firm_015, Firm_062, Firm_034, Firm_030, Firm_003, Firm_073, Firm_008, Firm_072) each appear in only one cited case, so the evidence here does not show them as repeat co-developers. These are coOccursWith style joint-development relationships rather than any directional dependsOn or enablesCapability link, so nothing in this set indicates one firm relying on or enabling another's capability, only that they worked together as manufacturers on the same census process.
